The present application has been filed under Section 430 read with Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, seeking suspension of sentence till pendency of his appeal.

2. Appellant, along with three other co-accused persons, was sent to face trial for commission of offences under Sections 498A/302/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and was convicted thereunder.

The appellant has preferred the captioned appeal seeking quashing/setting aside of the judgment of conviction dated 11.03.2025 and order on sentence dated 19.04.2025, passed by learned Trial Court in Sessions Case No. 7129/2016 arising out of FIR No. 214/2011, registered at Police Station Fatehpur Beri, Delhi, whereby appellant has been held guilty for offences punishable under Sections 498-A/302/34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and has been, inter alia, sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for life.
3. The victim, Smt. Neelam, was the daughter-in-law of the appellant.
The prosecution alleged that all the accused persons had subjected the victim to cruelty and had caused her death by setting her on fire.

4.

Earlier, while granting interim suspension of sentence, we took note of the fact that there was no specific allegation attributable to him and even the dying declaration, on which the prosecution places reliance, does not implicate him.

His mere presence in the house at the time of the incident,
by itself, seems to have been treated as sufficient to infer a shared common intention with the co-accused persons, despite the absence of any corroborating material.

sentences.text: Learned Counsel for appellant submits that appellant, who is 83 years of age, was a destitute daily-wage labourer, with no criminal antecedents.

She submits that the appellant is also suffering from multiple age-related ailments, including Hypertension, uncontrolled Type-II Diabetes Mellitus, diminution of vision in both the eyes on account of cataract, recurrent episodes of chest discomfort, urinary complications and severe osteo-arthritic pain.
She also submits that during the period of interim suspension of sentence, the appellant had been taken to hospital on several occasions for ophthalmic as well as general medical treatment.

However, in view of his uncontrolled blood pressure, uncontrolled blood sugar levels and other ailments, the advised surgery could not be undertaken, as the risk of intraoperative bleeding, cardiovascular complications and retinal damage was assessed to be high.
In these circumstances, she prays, the sentence of the appellant be suspended till pendency of appeal in order to enable him to avail specialized treatment and proper care outside the jail.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 03/12/2025 at 21:48:12 6.

Learned APP for the State, while vehemently opposing the present application, submits that the appellant stands convicted for a heinous offence and on an earlier occasion when his sentence was suspended for a period six weeks by this Court vide Order dated 10.09.2025, the appellant failed to surrender on the stipulated date, thereby violating the concession granted to him.

Having regard to the nature of the offence, the manner in which it was committed and his past conduct while availing interim suspension of sentence, the present application of the appellant may be dismissed.
7. In rebuttal, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has never wilfully violated the terms of surrender.

She contends that due to a sudden and severe deterioration in his health condition, the appellant was medically unfit to present himself on the scheduled date,
resulting in a brief delay of six days in surrendering.
She submits that such brief delay was bonafide and unintentional, and therefore ought not to be viewed as a deliberate attempt to evade the process of law.
8. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as learned APP for the State and have carefully perused the record.
9. The perusal of the Nominal Roll reveals that overall conduct of the appellant in jail has been recorded as satisfactory, where he is not, even, allotted any labour work due to his old age.

10. Keeping in mind the abovesaid aspects, his age and to enable the him to obtain specialized treatment and proper care, the sentence awarded to the appellant is hereby suspended, on his furnishing personal bond in a sum of Rs. 25,000/-, with one surety in like amount, subject to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court and further subject to the following conditions:

Appellant shall not leave the country without prior permission of the learned Trial Court and shall surrender his passport, if any,
before the learned Trial Court.
In case, he does not possess any passport, he shall state so before the learned Trial Court, by way of affidavit.
ii. Appellant shall provide his residential address, contact details and mobile numbers to the learned Trial Court.

In case of any change in their residential address and other contact details, the appellant shall immediately intimate the learned Trial Court by way of an affidavit as well as to the concerned SHO/IO, so that as and when the appeal is taken up for hearing, he shall be duly intimated.
Such contact details shall also be, in the same manner, furnished with the Registry of this Court and would form part of Appeal-Record.
iii. Appellant shall not indulge in any criminal activity during the period of suspension of sentence.

11. Accordingly, the present applications stand disposed of in aforesaid terms.
12. A copy of this Order be sent to learned Trial Court and the Jail Superintendent for information and necessary compliance.
13. List in due course.
VIVEK CHAUDHARY, J MANOJ JAIN, J DECEMBER 2, 2025/
